title: Government air-to-air FLIR expert's email on Gimbal rotation
summary: Marik von Rennenkampf tells of Government air-to-air FLIR expert's email on Gimbal rotation, about 2015 (video); email c. 2024 at Off the US East Coast (Roosevelt, 2014 to 2015), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Off the US East Coast (Gimbal video)

tellings.quote: I'll read it. The object in the video is definitely maneuvering causing the appearance of rotation.
I mean, Mick, we were on on the call with the AT Flare expert. He says, "This is quote bizarre. I've never seen anything like this."
tellings.difference: Quotes the expert on a call calling the video 'bizarre' and unlike anything he had seen, rather than reading an email about the object maneuvering.
tellings.link_reason: Both concern the government ATFLIR expert whom merrick consulted about the Gimbal video and who judged the object anomalous.

plain: Gimbal is a video filmed off the US East Coast around 2015 by an infrared camera on a Navy jet, the kind of camera called FLIR, which sees heat. It shows an object that seems to rotate, and people argue over whether the object really turns or whether the camera makes it look that way. During a debate on the podcast of a host, Jesse Michels, an analyst named Marik von Rennenkampf reads an email from a government expert in this kind of camera footage, who writes that the object is definitely maneuvering, causing the look of rotation. If so, the turning would be the object's own movement, not a camera trick. A second debater, Merrick, says he and others were on a call with the same expert, who called the video bizarre and said he had never seen anything like it. They make the point to a well-known skeptic, Mick West.
